newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dollar seen top-heavy, range-bound in Asia.
newsitem.headline: Dollar seen top-heavy, range-bound in Asia.

text.p: The dollar is expected to be range-bound during Asian trading time on Monday but top-heavy and with a slight downward bias after falling sharply against the mark in overseas Friday trade.

But activity is likely to be thin ahead of the meeting of Group of Seven (G7) finance ministers and central bank heads this coming weekend, with operators especially reluctant to take the dollar higher, dealers said.
Although further sales of dollars for marks may take the greenback down against the yen as well, support is expected from importer and institutional investor bids.

"We're likely to start seeing investor bids this week in connection with fresh overseas investment this new fiscal year," one trust bank dealer said, adding that these bids were likely to emerge around 125.30 yen.

The dollar slid against the mark on Friday after Market News Service cited unnamed officials of Germany's Christian Democratic Union Party as saying French President Jacques Chirac was withdrawing support for Italy in its drive to become a founding member of European economic and monetary union (EMU). But a French government source later denied the report and Italy reiterated its desire to join EMU in the first round.

As a result, the mark is expected to be strong against not only the dollar but also the yen, with further short-covering likely to weigh on the dollar versus the mark but support the dollar against the yen, dealers said.
Some exporter sales of dollars for yen are likely in connection with book-squaring ahead of a Japanese holiday next Tuesday.

But trade is otherwise expected to be quiet amid a lack of fresh factors on Monday. Although a Bank of Japan (BOJ) branch managers' meeting will be held on Monday and Tuesday, little impact is expected.
